To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hierarchically-cooled Ir NSs, and bimetal Ir-Rh NS and Rh NSs were successfully synthesized by a solid-liquid heterogeneous system and exhibited high selectivities towards azoxybenzine in the reduction of nitro benzene to azoxy benzine under ambient conditions.
hierarchically-coil ultrathin noble metal NSs with high surface area were successfully synthesized via a benzyl alcohol solvo-thermal route.
hierarchically-coil-shaped ultrathin noble metal nanosheet catalysts with high selectivity for the reduction of nitroarenes to azoxyarenes were synthesized using a benzyl alcohol solothermal method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of free-standing 2D noble metal nanosheet materials, which can be used as catalysts for the selective reduction of aromatic nitro compounds to azoxybenzenes.
a new approach for the preparation of free-standing fcc metal NSs and the development of a highly selective catalyst for the reduction of nitro compounds under ambient conditions.
the fabrication of atom-layer fcc metal NSs with high selectivity for nitrobenzine reduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has demonstrated the synthesis and application of atomically thin noble metal NSs with high surface area, which is an important step towards the development of atom-layered 2D noble metal NSs for various applications.
the hierarchically-coil-like structure of the 2D fcc metal NSs is the key to the selective reduction of PhNO to PhNHOH.
the free-standing hierarchically-coil Ir and Rh NSs with a fcc structure are highly selective for the reduction of nitro compounds to azoxy compounds under mild conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the solid-liquid interface-mediated 2D growth strategy could provide a new avenue for the preparation of 2D fcc noble metal NSs with a high surface energy and high surface-to-volume ratio, which are promising for the selective catalysis of organic molecules.

the hierarchically-coiling ultrathin fcc noble metal NSs with a large surface area, high surface energy, and abundant active sites can be obtained by using the benzyl-alcohol-mediated solvothermal approach, which provides a promising strategy for the synthesis of 2D fcc noble metal nanosheet catalysts.

we have demonstrated a facile approach to the fabrication of free-standing 2D noble metal NSs with a high selectivity towards the reduction of nitroarene, which could be extended for the development of other 2D noble metals with a high selectivities towards the reduction of other nitroarenes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2D growth strategy provides a facile and efficient route for the synthesis of free-standing 2D fcc noble metal NSs and the resultant 2D NSs with a high surface area are promising for catalysis.
the 2D growth of fcc noble metal NSs can be achieved by a solid-liquid interfacial reaction, which provides a new strategy to synthesize atomically thin fcc noble metal nanomaterials.
a solid-liquid heterogeneous system can be used to produce free-standing atom-layered fcc noble metal NSs, which are highly stable and active towards selective nitrobenzine reduction.
